03 / YOUR THINGS SHOULD STAY YOURS

A room of
your own.

A personal inn, with an open door when you want to leave. We’re designing for readable exports, local capture, and optional encrypted sync to your own private GitHub repository.

Start with yourself.

No feed. No audience. No pressure to turn every thought into something to share.

Take your things with you.

Portable notes and original attachments are part of the brief. Leaving should be as clear as arriving.

Quiet by default.

No unsolicited nudges. Find something when you need it, or revisit a few things on your own terms.

These are product commitments under development. Encrypted sync, export, and durable storage are not implemented in this design preview.

A FEW THINGS BEFORE YOU SETTLE IN

At the front desk.

Can I use Paste Inn today?+

You can explore the design and try saving notes and links for the current browser session. This is an early prototype: reloading clears those test saves. Please don’t use it as your only copy of anything important yet.

Will it work on my phone?+

The first product is planned as a responsive, installable web app. iPhone, Android, and desktop clients can follow once the core web experience works well. The preview already adapts to smaller screens.

Do I need a GitHub account?+

Not to explore this preview. The intended app should work locally before connecting storage. Optional encrypted sync through a private GitHub repository is planned, with setup and recovery still being designed.

What’s a chest?+

A possible name for an optional personal collection. Put related saves together if it helps; leave everything in the inbox if it doesn’t. Shared chests and group inns are future ideas.

What about a saved reel or YouTube video?+

The first version is intended to keep the link, your note, and an optional screenshot. It won’t promise a permanent downloaded copy of every video. Large media storage is being considered separately from GitHub sync.
